summary: A peak is strictly bigger than both neighbours, a valley strictly smaller. We check every element except the two ends, add peaks and valleys separately, and print the difference (T5 — neighbour comparison).

blocks.title: Read the array
blocks.text: N on one line, then all N numbers on the next line, split and turned into `int`s.

blocks.title: Two running sums
blocks.text: `peaks = valleys = 0` starts both totals at 0 in one line (safe for numbers).

blocks.title: Skip the first and last element
blocks.text: `range(1, N - 1)` visits indexes 1 to N-2, the only ones with BOTH neighbours. Including index 0 would compare with `arr[-1]`, the last element.

blocks.title: Peak: bigger than both sides
blocks.text: Strict `>` on both sides — an element equal to a neighbour (a plateau) is not a peak.

blocks.title: Valley: smaller than both sides
blocks.text: `elif` because an element can't be both. Again strict `<`.

pitfalls: Including the first or last element.
